title: Helping trumpeter Nick find his sound
summary: At UVA, a lead trumpeter finds a note with real sound; Baron notes you cannot sit next to Cootie Williams now.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: techniques. I mean and it’s just about getting them to get a sound. I remember one time I was at UVA uh, the Commonwealth, with Doug Richards, a great teacher down there, he had me there for a week. And there was this lead trumpet player, Nick, he had the most beautiful sound. But there was nothing inside the sound, it was just beautiful. Physically you learn how to do it. And just ideas would come to me, like these movement ideas and stuff, leaning the stomach against the hand, and all kinds of stuff. So a couple of times, he hit a note that was him, and you could feel it in the room and it was like wow. And that sound just like blew up. I mean I’m not freaking out but I’m going like wow. It took me a long time to really believe, sort of like you remember “The Music Man?” The Think System?
It’s really similar to that. I mean it’s an internal thing. Because you can’t sit next to Cootie Williams for six or seven nights a week for a year, now, you know you can’t. So I feel really blessed.
Yeah. You got on the tail end of that.
